notes.title: Keep the next instruction in view
notes.detail: The live response now appears immediately below the sentence instead of after every explanation card. On shorter iPad screens the layout is more compact, and the app gently brings the new instruction into view when needed.

notes.match: not really telling me what to do
notes.title: A clear practice path
notes.detail: Practice now begins with two numbered choices: first explore one English sentence without a score, then try the next small challenge. Review, speed and lesson-specific choices remain available under More practice choices.

notes.title: Shorter, varied practice
notes.detail: Rounds now have at most five questions, with varied verb positions. Three accurate, independent answers in under six seconds across different patterns can finish a round early. Speed alone never unlocks a new concept. Determiners, pronouns and prepositions follow the familiar word groups.

notes.title: Clearer grammar detail
notes.detail: Word-type detail uses >, such as determiner > article. Sentence jobs are shown separately as Job: subject or Job: object, because a subject is not a subtype of noun.

notes.title: History in plain language
notes.detail: The medieval period is explained as approximately 500–1500 CE in European history. The loose Japanese comparison has been removed; matching English, Latin and French examples now have their own page.

notes.title: Explain unfamiliar history words
notes.detail: Mesopotamia, century, millennium and Germanic languages now have child-friendly explanations. Century blocks show how ten centuries make one millennium.

notes.title: Find Rome on a map
notes.detail: A factual map highlights modern Lazio in Italy and marks Rome. The caption distinguishes modern Lazio from the smaller ancient region of Latium.

notes.title: A visible feedback trail
notes.detail: Matching notes from 3.0.1 are ticked as implemented, moved below open notes and linked to these release notes. Editing the request reopens it. Notes can also be archived and restored.

notes.title: English first, then compare
notes.detail: Three responsive columns compare the same meaning in English, Latin and French. Separate examples explain word order, adjective agreement and I love without assuming prior grammar knowledge.

notes.title: Editable notes and a familiar close button
notes.detail: Saving clears the input. Existing notes can be edited. The dialog has a top-right ×, a Done button and Escape support. Unsaved text is retained as a draft.

notes.title: Automatic reconnection and complete cloud records
notes.detail: After the first parent sign-in, the app restores the Firebase session, pulls saved data on opening and retries on reconnect. Notes, drafts, settings, progress and recorded attempts sync in separate records so older recordings are not silently dropped to fit one document. Sync status is visible; no password is copied into app data.
